wa_full_or_nearly_wall_routes.blurb: These long lines run up the tallest stretch of the Upper Town Wall above the town of Index, in the Skykomish Valley west of Stevens Pass. Most are multi-pitch, typically three to seven pitches, and the mix is traditional leads, aid ascents and a handful of bolted lines, about two dozen in all. Difficulty sits well up the scale: a couple of easier lines near 5.7, then a solid block of 5.11 and 5.12, with a few 5.13 test pieces at the top end. This is a place for experienced parties comfortable on sustained, committing wall terrain and carrying a full rack, not a casual afternoon cragging stop.

wa_diamond_the_2.blurb: The Diamond is a big cliff at Index, in the Skykomish Valley, standing over Duck Wall and just east of the Cheeks. Routes here are a blend of traditional and bolted lines, with a few aid pitches and a single boulder problem, around two dozen in total. Grades start in the 5.8 range and cluster heavily in 5.11, with a few 5.12 and one 5.13, so it suits climbers who already lead solidly. Several lines are multi-pitch, and the stone around Index is steep and featured with plenty of holds. Reaching the base means a steep gully or a trail along the foot of the Cheeks, which runs wet in spring.

wa_fat_and_skinny_man_walls.blurb: Fat Man and Skinny Man are neighbouring walls in the Echo Basin section of Vantage (Frenchman Coulee), tucked below the east end of Sunshine Wall. Nearly all of the two dozen routes are bolted sport climbs, with a couple of trad options. They are short but steep and crimpy, with several starting off bouldery moves before easing to face climbing higher. Most climbing falls in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with just a few easier or harder outings, so it fits climbers working through the intermediate-to-advanced sport grades. Both walls are basalt, and Skinny Man begins to the right of Fat Man at an overhanging corner.

wa_club_paradiso_the_actual_cave.blurb: Club Paradiso and the Actual Cave sit in the woods on Mt Washington near North Bend, in the Snoqualmie Valley. All 25 routes are bolted sport climbs. The cave is a small, steep, horizontal feature with short, gymnastic lines, mostly 5.11 to 5.12 with a handful of 5.13, while the neighbouring Club Paradiso wall holds some easier juggy lines between roughly 5.8 and 5.10. The cave faces north, stays cool and shaded, and can hold seepage for much of the year, so it works as a hot-day destination; the milder lines can stay wet in a damp year. Falls near the ground are a real possibility on the short routes.

wa_purina_crags.blurb: Purina Crags is a cluster of small cliffs in the lower Icicle Creek canyon outside Leavenworth, on the way to Careno Crag. Mostly single-pitch, it is dominated by traditional crack and face routes, with a few bolted lines mixed in. Grades range from about 5.7 up to a 5.12, and the bulk of climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.10, making it a friendly place to build trad skills. The walls face mainly south and east, so they warm up quickly and dry out earlier than higher parts of the canyon, which makes them a good early or late season choice, though midsummer can be hot. Look for the big roof on the main cliff.
wa_purina_crags.parking_note: Leave the car along the road opposite the Snow Creek trailhead lot, then walk the short path leading up to the cliffs.

wa_madsen_s_buttress.blurb: Madsen's Buttress is a group of small crags in lower Icicle Creek near Leavenworth, directly across the road from the Snow Creek trailhead lot. The best-known feature is a bold overhanging roof called the Visor, and a number of routes here are quiet compared with other Icicle walls. About two dozen routes mix traditional leads, sport lines and one aid route. Difficulty spans from 5.6 or so up to a few 5.12 and 5.13 climbs, but the largest share sits around 5.9 to 5.11, so there is something for climbers stepping up from easier terrain as well as stronger leaders. Approaches are short, a brief climb up from the road.
wa_madsen_s_buttress.parking_note: Park at or near the Snow Creek trailhead area on Icicle Road; the crags lie just over the road from it.

wa_snow_creek_wall.blurb: Snow Creek Wall is a tall mountain face of about 800 feet above Icicle Creek near Leavenworth, and it is the region's premier multi-pitch trad objective. All of the two dozen or so routes here are traditional leads, many of six to eight pitches, with cracks, faces and knobs to help along the way. Grades run mostly 5.7 to 5.11, stretching to 5.13 at the top, and local ratings are considered stiff. Expect a long uphill approach through the woods and a long walk-off, so plan for a full day. It is busy on summer weekends and hot in midsummer, making spring and fall the favoured seasons.
wa_snow_creek_wall.parking_note: Drive Icicle Road west out of Leavenworth for roughly four miles to the Snow Creek trailhead lot, where the hike to the wall begins.
wa_snow_creek_wall.approach: Follow the Snow Creek trail uphill, then cut off right to cross the creek on a log. Scramble up boulders and talus to a climber's trail that climbs steeply to the base of the wall.

wa_lava_wall_deadheads.blurb: Lava Wall and Deadheads form the main wall at Lava Point, a sport crag on the Tieton River near Rimrock Lake. It is a long, south-facing shelf that gets taller and steeper toward the left, reached by an easy trail through open woods and meadows. All two dozen routes are bolted sport climbs, from 5.9 up to 5.12, with half of them in the 5.11 range, mostly vertical to slightly overhanging on textured edges, jugs and pockets. Afternoon shade arrives on the wall, but summer still runs hot, and it can open early in the year after a low-snow winter. Ledges at the base call for some care.
